studies.label: Classroom experiment: GenAI-supported vs peer-collaborative vs individual creative writing (fifth graders, China)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract, Methods; random assignment and arm counts confirmed in PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; analyzed arm counts confirmed in PDF p. 7, Table 1
counts_source.quote:
An experiment involved 78 primary school students in China assigned to three conditions: GenAI-­supported writing 
(n = 20), peer collaboration (n = 38; 19 pairs), and individual writing (n = 20).

arms.name: GenAI-supported writing group
arms.description: Students used Deepseek on computers during the creative writing task after a tutorial. They were instructed to use it as a thinking partner, evaluate and adapt suggestions, and avoid verbatim copying; final essays were handwritten (PDF pp. 4-6, Sections 3.1-3.3).

arms.name: Peer-collaborative writing group
arms.description: Students collaborated with a peer in 19 pairs and produced handwritten creative writing. Table 1 counts 38 students, but the paper does not establish the number of distinct essays or how partner scores were entered (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 5, Figure 1; PDF p. 7, Table 1).

arms.name: Individual writing group
arms.description: Students completed the same creative writing task independently by hand, without AI assistance (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.1-3.2 and Figure 1).

studies.task: Fifth-grade students wrote an essay, Design Future Cars, of around 300 words within 25 minutes during the second-week classroom session (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.3).

ai_tool.name: Deepseek (model version not stated)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.3: "The GenAI tool used in this study was Deepseek." The model version and release year are not stated.

estimates.outcome: Creative writing performance (rubric total score, out of 100)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Three researchers independently rated the handwritten essays on a rubric with originality (40 points), flexibility (30), and elaboration (30), for a total possible score of 100. When inter-rater agreement was high the raters' average was used, and when low the raters discussed scores to consensus; the second-week ratings were described as satisfactory. The explicit consensus procedure concerns the first-week baseline. Only the total rubric score is reported, and rater blinding is not stated (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.3-3.4).

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports participant-indexed arm means, SDs, and N. The source quotes preserve the printed three-decimal precision. The LSD post hoc comparison indicates that the AI arm scored significantly higher, but the paper prints no numerical pairwise difference, SE, CI, test statistic, p-value, or standardized effect. The omnibus ANOVA statistics concern all arms and are inventoried in the paper-level notes, not assigned to either pairwise contrast. se_basis=participant identifies the participant-indexed summaries and analysis; it does not imply that a pairwise SE was printed. The combined count for this particular contrast is not printed, so n_total is null; no count or effect was calculated. Each student in these two arms completed the writing task individually; the AI arm used Deepseek during production (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.1-3.2 and Figure 1).

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports participant-indexed arm means, SDs, and N. The source quotes preserve the printed three-decimal precision. The LSD post hoc comparison indicates that the AI arm scored significantly higher, but the paper prints no numerical pairwise difference, SE, CI, test statistic, p-value, or standardized effect. The omnibus ANOVA statistics concern all arms and are inventoried in the paper-level notes, not assigned to either pairwise contrast. se_basis=participant identifies the participant-indexed summaries and analysis; it does not imply that a pairwise SE was printed. The combined count for this particular contrast is not printed, so n_total is null; no count or effect was calculated. The peer arm contains 38 students working in 19 pairs (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 5, Figure 1), whereas Table 1 uses N=38. unit, sd_level, and se_basis follow the paper's nominal participant-level analysis. It is unclear whether partners share one essay and whether its score was entered for both students. No adjustment for partner or classroom dependence is described. Independence of the peer scores must be resolved before treating the nominal participant-based precision as valid. The number of distinct essays is not stated, so n_units is null.

not_extracted.reason: Descriptive process analysis of the AI arm only, with no between-arm contrast. Prompt categories describe requests to the tool, and uptake codes describe incorporation of AI content rather than an eligible creativity or across-people diversity outcome (PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 3.4 and 4.4 and Table 4).

not_extracted.what: Creative writing performance: Peer-collaborative writing group versus Individual writing group
not_extracted.reason: Table 1 reports the LSD ordering b > c, but neither arm received generative AI. This contrast falls outside the required AI-versus-comparison-arm contrasts (PDF p. 7, Table 1 and Section 4.1).

open_items: Peer-arm dependence: the paper reports 38 students working in 19 pairs but analyzes N=38 (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Table 1). Whether partners submitted a shared essay, whether scores were duplicated across partners, and how this affects the reported SD and post hoc precision are not stated. No pair-level adjustment is described; participant-indexed coding is provisional for the peer contrast.

No numerical pairwise mean differences, SEs, CIs, test statistics, p-values, or standardized effects are printed. Table 1 supplies only the LSD orderings for pairwise inference; its F, p, partial eta-squared, and Cohen's f concern the complete three-arm comparison.
The number of people in each pairwise contrast is not printed as a combined total; n_total is null rather than calculated from the arm counts.
The Deepseek model version and release year are not stated (PDF p. 5, Section 3.3); ai_tool.year is null.
Random assignment of participants is explicit, but sequence generation, handling of the original classes, and the unequal allocation are not explained (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).
The researchers' blinding to writing condition is not stated (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.3-3.4).
Only the total creativity rubric score is reported. Separate originality, flexibility, and elaboration scores, and baseline arm summaries, would require additional data.
No preregistration or designated primary outcome is stated. The data are available only from the corresponding author upon reasonable request (PDF p. 11, Data Availability Statement).
notes:
The complete markdown conversion was read through the references. The PDF has no appendix; no separate supplement is referenced or listed on file. The main-text supplementary analysis in Sections 3.4 and 4.4 and Table 4 was reviewed. Tables 1-4 and Figure 1 were checked first, and every page supporting extracted numbers was examined with pymupdf. Figures and passages missing from the PDF text layer were checked using in-memory renders of PDF pp. 5, 7, and 8; no image or auxiliary file was saved. The eligible-outcome statistic inventory is the arm N, Mean, and SD in Table 1 (transcribed into the two estimates), plus the following omnibus and assumption-test statistics. Table 1 (PDF p. 7) reports F=13.095, p=0.000***, partial η2=0.259, and Cohen's f=0.591 for all three groups together. The table footnote states ***p<0.001. The table's numerical block, copied from the PDF, is "13.095
0.000***
0.259
0.591
a > b
a > c
b > c". Its LSD column gives a>b, a>c, and b>c; no numerical pairwise test is printed. Section 4.1 (PDF p. 7, rendered page) repeats the omnibus result as "(F = 13.095, p < 0.05)" and states "The Levene test value of creative writing scores was 0.397 (>0.05)". Neither the omnibus p-value nor the omnibus effect sizes are used as pairwise statistics. Field RCT coding follows the use of ordinary classroom hours and the familiar school computer laboratory (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.1-3.2). The randomization statement is "Participants were randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions" (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1); the original classes and the peer pairs are not reported as assignment clusters. The analyzed count uses the full study sample, with the same arm counts in Table 1 as at assignment; no attrition or exclusions of students are reported. Although the task leaned toward expository and informational writing (PDF p. 10), the eligible score explicitly rates originality, flexibility, and elaboration rather than general writing proficiency (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4). No across-people diversity or post-AI unaided outcome is reported. No shared sample with another paper is stated; the related Yang, Liu, and Gao paper is cited for intervention duration (PDF p. 10), not identified as sharing participants. Extractor B used the reconciled screening form only as a map and did not read extractor A's extraction. All effect statistics were transcribed; no standardized effect, mean difference, SE, CI, or contrast total was computed.
